parts.text: I only see one Nimbus findings comment on PR #20 (it was edited), so there isn’t a separate previous findings message visible via the PR comments API.
You checked for it within this chat history, look there

From this chat history, the previous findings message was this 3-item list:

- `[medium/security/single]` Trusted PR detection used `pr?.head?.repo?.fork === false`, which could treat fork PRs as trusted when `fork` is missing/undefined; suggested stricter check.
- `[low/logic/single]` Workflow passed `--base "${BASE_REF}"` and `--output-review-id`; `BASE_REF` format (`origin/${base.ref}`) could be inconsistent if ref has special chars or fetch fails.
- `[low/logic/single]` Review ID file write fallback to `process.cwd()` (if git root detection fails) could write to unexpected location in CI instead of `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`.
That’s literally also the current message on the PR right now. Why do you think that it’s not the same?

You’re right — it *is* the same findings content.

I said “no” earlier because I checked PR metadata and only saw one comment record (with an `updatedAt` timestamp), so I interpreted your question as “is there a separate new comment object after a new review?” rather than “did the findings text change?”.  
Given the content is identical, the correct interpretation is: no new/different findings message was posted, just the same comment instance.
Why could this be happening? I am starting to feel like we should move away from this experience because the PR comment does not get updated consistently at all

Totally fair frustration. What you’re seeing is a common failure mode with “sticky PR comment” workflows.

Most likely causes:

- Marker-based upsert is brittle: if the workflow searches for `<!-- nimbus-review-comment -->` and doesn’t find exactly one match (pagination, filtering, minimized comments, author mismatch), it may create/update inconsistently.
- Concurrent runs race each other: two workflow runs on the same PR can both read old state, then one edits while the other posts or overwrites.
- Different identity/token contexts: comments created by `github-actions[bot]` vs a GitHub App/token can break “find my previous comment” logic.
- Trigger mismatch: `pull_request`, `pull_request_target`, and manual dispatch runs may have different permissions and see/update comments differently.
- Edit path succeeds but content looks unchanged: run metadata updates (`updatedAt`) while findings body stays the same, which feels like “not updated.”
- API selection issues: using a single `pr view comments` call may miss edge cases unless you explicitly query issue comments with pagination and strict matching.

If you want a more reliable UX, I’d strongly recommend this direction:

1. Keep PR comments only for first-time “anchor” post.
2. Put per-run findings in a Check Run (`gh api repos/:owner/:repo/check-runs`) with rich summary.
3. Link the latest Check Run from the anchor comment instead of rewriting large bodies every run.
4. Add workflow concurrency guard:  
   `concurrency: { group: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-nimbus-review, cancel-in-progress: true }`
5. Make upsert deterministic: list all issue comments, filter by marker + exact bot author, sort by `created_at`, edit newest one only.

That gives you stable history + a single reliable “latest status” surface (Checks tab), which is usually much less flaky than repeated comment edits.
Go ahead and build it just to see

[medium/security/single] The workflow step 'Refresh PR base ref' executes git fetch using user-controlled input from github.event.pull_request.base.ref without sanitization. This allows PR authors to inject arbitrary git references, potentially fetching unintended branches or triggering remote code execution if combined with git hooks or malicious refs. This will accumulate noise comments on PRs from forks or failed runs. (.github/workflows/nimbus-pr-review.yml:142-180)
